title: Rep. María Elvira Salazar highlights local service academy event and condemns Cuban repression

Rep. María Elvira Salazar highlights local service academy event and condemns Cuban repression
U.S. Rep. María Elvira Salazar used recent posts from late September and early October to promote a local service academy information day while also drawing attention to trials against dissidents in Cuba—specifically mentioning Anna Bensi and her...
Rep. María Elvira Salazar, U.S. Representative for Florida's 27th congressional district, posted a series of tweets highlighting both an upcoming educational event in her district and concerns over human rights conditions in Cuba.
On September 29, 2026, Salazar invited students and families to an informational event: "For students called to serve On October 7, I’m hosting Service Academy Day in Coral Gables for students and families interested in pursuing an education at one of our nation’s U.S. Service Academies. Come meet representatives, learn about the admissions process, and find out https://t.co/pfbnaw4Yx2". The event aims to provide information on admission processes to U.S. Service Academies.
Turning her attention to international affairs on October 1, Salazar addressed the situation in Cuba regarding Anna Bensi and her mother Caridad: "Today, 21-year-old Anna Bensi and her mother, Caridad, are facing trial in Havana, while State Security surrounds the homes of journalists and activists trying to attend. As the Cuban dictatorship collapses under the weight of its own failures, repression is all it has left. But https://t.co/KBJajKFfCd".
Shortly after that post on the same day, she reiterated her message in Spanish: "Hoy, Anna Bensi, de apenas 21 años, y su madre, Caridad, enfrentan un juicio en La Habana, mientras la Seguridad del Estado vigila las casas de periodistas y activistas que intentan acompañarlas. Mientras la dictadura cubana se derrumba bajo el peso de sus propios fracasos, la https://t.co/FyHBpcCjC1".
Salazar has been an outspoken critic of human rights abuses by the Cuban government and frequently highlights issues affecting Cuban dissidents through her social media platforms.
